title: Uniqueness of harmonic Lagrangian circle-field extensions with bounded antiholomorphic derivative on the hyperbolic plane
source_title: Mean surfaces in half-pipe space and infinitesimal Teichmüller theory
author: Farid Diaf
difficulty_reason: The scalar Plateau uniqueness theorem does not identify the boundary support function from a vector-field trace alone. The author converts bounded antiholomorphic derivative into bounded shape operator, constructs convex and concave shifts with a common continuous boundary value, and then recovers the vector trace using the full canonical-extension geometric construction. This boundary-identification argument is the nonroutine remaining obligation beyond the precise prior scalar PDE and harmonic-field foundations.

proof_review.note: Full article retained as conservative closed context for notation, global assumptions, diagrams and references. Exact primary and supporting physical proof pages are recorded separately. Continuous circle vector field X; harmonic Lagrangian V on H2 extending continuously to X and with finite sup norm of the antiholomorphic derivative tensor. Then V equals the canonical mean-surface extension HL(X). The boundedness condition is essential and retained. Full uniqueness and convex normal-translation core47–49 read; harmonic Lagrangian potential characterization26–32, shape/derivative identity32–33, and boundary extension new core39–44 read. Published Barbot–Fillastre mean-surface Dirichlet existence/uniqueness20, Li–Yau40 and infinitesimal earthquake boundary extension Dia24 Proposition4.6 are named prerequisites. The identification with Douady–Earle is unnecessary for this equality to HL and is not selected. No width estimates or little-Zygmund variant counted.

historical_source_pdf_evidence.original_difficulty_reason: The author turns a bounded tensor condition into convex and concave normal translates of a half-pipe mean surface, proves its boundary continuity, and identifies the boundary vector field through a Li–Yau-controlled extension. This geometric boundary uniqueness exceeds qualifying-exam differential geometry.
